basic_info.name: Suzanne Treister
basic_info.active_years: 1980s-present (pioneer in digital/new media art since early 1990s; painting practice from 1980s)
basic_info.location: London, UK and French Pyrenees (born London, 1958)

practice_description.medium: Drawing, watercolour, diagrammatic mapping, tarot decks, video, installation, photography, web-based work
practice_description.practice_summary: Suzanne Treister creates extensive multi-part projects that map hidden connections between technology, power, knowledge, and belief systems through hand-drawn diagrams, alchemical illustrations, and tarot decks. Her work reveals structures that bind power, identity, and knowledge by tracing how information flows through officially unconnected networks across decades of history.
practice_description.methodology: Treister conducts years-long research investigations spanning cybernetics, military history, counterculture, surveillance, science fiction, occult traditions, and emerging technologies. She synthesizes this research into elaborate taxonomies rendered in traditional media — drawing, watercolour, and diagrammatic illustration — deliberately using 'older technologies that I have autonomy over' rather than the digital systems she critiques. Her projects typically comprise hundreds of individual works organized through frameworks like the tarot (78 cards providing a combinatorial system for connecting disparate knowledge domains). The tarot structure functions as an 'encyclopedic format' and 'alchemical hypertext' that enables non-linear navigation of complex historical and technological relationships. She works across the boundary between scientific inquiry and mystical revelation, using speculative and occult knowledge forms to make visible connections that rational taxonomies obscure.

relevance_to_sense_room.relevance_summary: Treister's decades-long practice of mapping knowledge networks as art — using diagrams, tarot structures, and relational illustrations — is a foundational precedent for A(DAI)'s graph-curated exhibition concept. HEXEN 2.0 and HEXEN 5.0 demonstrate that a network of ideas, figures, and events can function as a major artwork where the relational structure is the primary content.
relevance_to_sense_room.art_as_substrate: Yes. Treister's diagrams and tarot systems function as substrates that viewers/participants navigate and activate. The HEXEN tarot decks are explicitly designed as tools — they can be used for collective readings that generate new configurations and interpretations of the mapped knowledge. The substrate is the knowledge network itself.
relevance_to_sense_room.relational_composition: Yes, fundamentally. The HEXEN projects are structured as webs of connections between figures, theories, events, and institutions. The five wall-scale diagrams in HEXEN 2.0 explicitly chart relational networks — 'web-like illustrations depicting key figures of the counter cultures which developed in concurrence with governmental technological developments.' The tarot format adds a combinatorial relational layer: each card's meaning shifts depending on its relationships to other cards in a reading.
relevance_to_sense_room.self_recomposing: Partially. The fixed artworks (diagrams, drawings) are static. However, the tarot decks are designed to be used as tools for collective readings — each reading produces a unique relational configuration. Treister explicitly describes the tarot readings as 'a deconstructionist game for analysing and assessing recent history, the present and imagining a future, done so as a collective.' This participatory use introduces a form of recomposition through human interaction, though it is not computational.

works.title: HEXEN 2.0
works.description: 167-part project comprising 5 large wall-scale diagrams, a 78-card tarot deck, photo-text works, video, and website. Maps the interconnected histories of cybernetics, the internet, military research, counterculture, surveillance, and the control society from WWII to the present. Each tarot card depicts a key figure, theory, or event. The diagrams trace how knowledge 'trips' through unofficially connected networks. Acquired by Tate. Exhibited at Science Museum London and internationally.
works.relevance: The most complete precedent for knowledge-network-as-artwork in the HEXEN tradition. Demonstrates that a hand-crafted graph of ideas and actors can function as a major museum-quality artwork. The tarot format shows how a fixed knowledge graph can generate infinite relational readings through combinatorial use — a non-computational analog to A(DAI)'s generative graph curation.

works.title: HEXEN 5.0
works.description: 78 tarot works, 6 large diagrams, and AI-prompted works reimagining alchemical visual language (13th-18th century). Addresses the climate emergency, AI, quantum science, and potential solutions for planetary self-regulation. Builds on HEXEN 2.0's methodology while engaging directly with contemporary AI and ecological crises. Published as a tarot deck by Cosmogenesis.
works.relevance: Demonstrates the ongoing vitality and adaptability of knowledge-network mapping as artistic practice. The direct engagement with AI and climate — two central concerns for A(DAI) — makes this the most thematically current precedent. The evolution from HEXEN 2.0 to 5.0 shows how a knowledge graph can be extended and updated over decades.

works.title: Prophetic Dreaming (retrospective)
works.description: First major institutional retrospective spanning 40+ years at Modern Art Oxford (October 2025-April 2026), travelling to Muzeum Sztuki Lodz (2026) and MIMA Middlesbrough (2027). Maps Treister's complete practice of investigating technologies, networks of power, alternative belief systems, and futures they prefigure.
works.relevance: The retrospective format itself demonstrates how a lifelong practice of knowledge mapping accumulates into a meta-graph — Treister's complete body of work IS a decades-spanning relational map of technology, power, and alternative futures.

protocol_art_resonance.protocol_art_summary: Treister does not design protocols or systems in a technical sense, but her tarot decks function as protocols for collective knowledge navigation. The HEXEN tarot system provides a structured method (draw cards, read relationships, generate interpretation) for groups to collectively analyze historical forces and imagine futures. This is protocol design in a social/participatory sense — creating rules and structures for collective sensemaking.
protocol_art_resonance.system_designed: The HEXEN tarot system — a combinatorial framework for collective readings that function as group sensemaking sessions. The framework includes 78 cards representing key nodes in a knowledge network, structured according to tarot's major/minor arcana system, designed to be used in group settings for analyzing the present and imagining futures. This is a social protocol for collective intelligence, not a technical one.

commons_orientation.commons_summary: Treister's work circulates through the commercial gallery system (represented by Annely Juda Fine Art, P.P.O.W. Gallery) and institutional collections (Tate, Centre Pompidou, Science Museum). However, significant parts of the work are freely accessible through her comprehensive website (suzannetreister.net) and the HEXEN project websites. The tarot decks are published as affordable objects (not limited editions). The knowledge-sharing ethos of the practice — making hidden connections visible — is commons-oriented in spirit, even when the physical artworks circulate commercially. [uncertain]

governance_model.governance_detail: Solo artistic practice spanning over 40 years. Treister is the sole author, researcher, and creator of all works. The tarot readings introduce a participatory governance element — when used collectively, the group's interpretive choices determine meaning — but the artworks themselves are authored by Treister alone.

consent_and_authorship.consent_approach: Not a primary concern for the practice. Treister works with historical and published material — mapping publicly known figures, events, institutions, and theories. No personal data or participant data is used. The tarot readings involve voluntary participation in collective interpretation.
consent_and_authorship.authorship_model: Solo authorship. Treister is the sole creator of all works, conducting all research and producing all drawings, diagrams, and illustrations herself. She deliberately chooses hand-drawing and watercolour as media she has full autonomy over, maintaining complete authorial control. No machine co-authorship (she explicitly eschews using AI to make work about AI).

liveness_and_duration.temporal_detail: Individual artworks are fixed — hand-drawn diagrams, watercolours, and prints that do not change. However, the tarot decks introduce a performative temporal dimension: each group reading produces a unique configuration in real-time. The practice itself has a durational quality — HEXEN evolved from 2.0 (2009-2011) to 5.0 (2023-2025), showing how a knowledge mapping project extends and recomposes across decades. The websites remain accessible as living reference documents.

data_materiality.data_sources: Historical research spanning cybernetics, military history, intelligence agencies, counterculture movements, science fiction, occult traditions, quantum science, AI research, climate science, philosophy, sociology, and political theory. Sources include published histories, declassified documents, academic research, biographical information about key figures, and speculative/fictional texts.
data_materiality.data_provenance: Entirely from published, public-domain, and historical sources. No scraped data, no personal data, no institutional datasets. The research is traditional scholarly/investigative work synthesized through artistic practice. Fully transparent provenance — all figures and events depicted are identifiable and verifiable.

embedding_space_relevance.embedding_summary: Treister does not work with computational embedding spaces. However, her practice is conceptually analogous: she manually 'embeds' historical figures, events, theories, and institutions in a relational space (the diagram) based on their connections and influences. The tarot structure provides a fixed dimensional framework (78 positions) within which knowledge is embedded. This is a human-authored, non-computational form of relational embedding.
embedding_space_relevance.multimodal: Works span visual (drawings, watercolours, diagrams), textual (research, card descriptions), video, and web modalities, but these are not computationally unified. They are complementary presentations of the same research program.

exhibition_modality.spatial_description: Works manifest as: (1) large wall-scale diagrams that viewers navigate physically, tracing connections across the surface, (2) framed watercolours and drawings arranged in grids or sequences, (3) tarot decks as portable, handleable objects used in collective readings, (4) video animations, (5) websites for digital navigation. The physical exhibition experience involves moving between wall diagrams and individual drawings, piecing together the relational network across the gallery space. The tarot deck can be used outside the gallery in participatory settings.

interoperability.composability: The tarot deck format is inherently composable — cards can be combined in infinite configurations for readings. The knowledge network depicted in the diagrams could theoretically be digitized into a graph database, though Treister has not done this. The content is highly composable at a conceptual level (figures, events, and connections could be integrated into larger knowledge systems) but is not technically interoperable in its current form.
interoperability.technical_openness: The artworks are physically open (exhibited, published, accessible on her website) but not technically open in the sense of APIs, standard formats, or machine-readable data. The knowledge is embedded in hand-drawn visual form rather than structured data.

technical_approach.stack: Traditional art media: drawing, watercolour, pen and ink. Video production tools. Web development for project websites. Photography. Treister deliberately avoids using the technologies she critiques — she uses 'older technologies like drawing and watercolour that I have autonomy over and are not dependent on the technologies I might be examining.' No ML, no generative software, no blockchain, no code-based art. The 'technology' is research methodology and the tarot's combinatorial structure.

network_position.scene_affiliation: Contemporary art (Tate, Centre Pompidou, Modern Art Oxford), new media art (pioneer since 1990s), critical technology art, digital culture critique, speculative/science fiction art, occult/esoteric art traditions. Bridges the contemporary art mainstream with critical technology discourse, and bridges rational/scientific analysis with esoteric/occult knowledge frameworks. Connected to London's art and technology scene, European new media art networks.
network_position.connections: Vladan Joler (shared practice of diagrammatic knowledge mapping as art — Joler maps technological infrastructure, Treister maps historical/political/occult knowledge networks; both use the relational diagram as primary artistic form and both are in major institutional collections). Both represent the 'graph-as-art' tradition that is the most direct precedent for A(DAI).

potential_role_in_adai.role_detail: Treister's practice provides A(DAI) with: (1) a 40-year precedent for knowledge-network mapping as a legitimate and major art form, (2) the tarot as a model for combinatorial knowledge navigation — a non-computational protocol for collective sensemaking through relational reading, (3) a critique of techno-solutionism from within the art-technology space (her refusal to use AI to discuss AI is a principled position A(DAI) should consider), (4) evidence that hand-crafted, human-authored knowledge graphs have enduring value (Tate acquisition, ongoing retrospective). HEXEN's evolution from 2.0 to 5.0 across 15 years shows how a knowledge mapping project can grow and adapt. Her tarot-based collective reading protocol could inspire A(DAI)'s approach to participatory knowledge navigation.
